feature: large gRPC unary payloads as borrowed HTTP/2 DATA prefix slices

scope.consumer: ordinary gRPC unary request and response paths
scope.small_message_behavior: unchanged single-allocation frame and combined HEADERS/DATA burst
scope.large_message_behavior: five-byte gRPC frame prefix on the stack plus the caller payload as ordered DATA slices

design.length_contract: all body-length validation, automatic Content-Length, and declared-length checks use body_prefix.len + body.len
design.response_path: HEADERS, ordered prefix/body DATA slices, then trailers under the original absolute deadline
design.request_path: suspended uploads retain prefix and body separately and resume the remaining prefix before the remaining body
design.batch_boundary: writeResponseBatch rejects a non-empty body_prefix because it serializes one contiguous body
design.head_boundary: HEAD suppression emits no DATA for prefix or body while retaining existing content-length rules

verification.full_library: 6179/6180 passed; the single shared caller-cancellation failure passed on focused rerun and was load-sensitive
verification.allocation_test: a 100,000-byte gRPC unary request and response through 4-KiB DATA frames made zero allocations at or above the payload size in writeUnaryResponse
verification.reverse_interop: interop-grpc-cpp-client EXIT=0 on rerun; the first run hit a transient status_code_and_message RST_STREAM CANCEL race under host load, and the same scenario passed on rerun

conclusion: Large ordinary gRPC unary calls no longer materialize a second payload-sized request or response staging buffer. The change preserves framing, content-length, trailers, HEAD, early-response upload, flow-control, and deadline behavior, and both grpc-cpp interop directions pass. No wall-time claim is made because the shared-channel benchmark uses duplex streams rather than the ordinary unary response path.
